From these observations it must appear unquestionably true, that 배심 재판 is in no case abolished by the 제안된 헌법, and it is equally true, that in those controversies between individuals in which the great body of the people are likely to be interested, that institution will remain precisely in the same situation in which it is placed by the State 헌법s, and will be in no degree altered or influenced by the adoption of the plan under consideration. The foundation of this assertion is, that the national 사법부 will have no cognizance of them, and of course they will remain determinable as heretofore by the State courts only, and in the manner which the State 헌법s and laws prescribe. All land causes, except where claims under the grants of different States come into question, and all other controversies between the citizens of the same State, unless where they depend upon positive violations of the articles of union, by acts of the State 입법부s, will belong exclusively to the 관할권 of the State 법정s. Add to this, that admiralty causes, and almost all those which are of equity 관할권, are determinable under our own 정부 without the intervention of a jury, and the inference from the whole will be, that this institution, as it exists with us at present, cannot possibly be affected to any great extent by the proposed alteration in our system of 정부.

The friends and adversaries of the plan of the convention, if they agree in nothing else, concur at least in the value they set upon the 배심 재판; or if there is any difference between them it consists in this: the former regard it as a valuable safeguard to 자유; the latter represent it as the very palladium of free 정부. For my own part, the more the operation of the institution has fallen under my observation, the more reason I have discovered for holding it in high estimation; and it would be altogether superfluous to examine to what extent it deserves to be esteemed useful or essential in a representative 공화국, or how much more merit it may be entitled to, as a defense against the oppressions of an hereditary monarch, than as a barrier to the 폭정 of popular 행정관s in a popular 정부. Discussions of this kind would be more curious than beneficial, as all are satisfied of the utility of the institution, and of its friendly aspect to 자유. But I must acknowledge that I cannot readily discern the inseparable connection between the existence of 자유, and the 배심 재판 in civil cases. Arbitrary 탄핵s, arbitrary methods of prosecuting pretended offenses, and arbitrary punishments upon arbitrary convictions, have ever appeared to me to be the great engines of judicial 전제정; and these have all relation to criminal proceedings. The 배심 재판 in criminal cases, aided by the habeas corpus act, seems therefore to be alone concerned in the question. And both of these are provided for, in the most ample manner, in the plan of the convention.
It has been observed, that 배심 재판 is a safeguard against an oppressive exercise of the power of 과세. This observation deserves to be canvassed.

It is evident that it can have no influence upon the 입법부, in regard to the amount of taxes to be laid, to the objects upon which they are to be imposed, or to the rule by which they are to be apportioned. If it can have any influence, therefore, it must be upon the mode of collection, and the conduct of the officers intrusted with the execution of the 세입 laws.

As to the mode of collection in this State, under our own Constitution, the 배심 재판 is in most cases out of use. The taxes are usually levied by the more summary proceeding of distress and sale, as in cases of rent. And it is acknowledged on all hands, that this is essential to the efficacy of the 세입 laws. The dilatory course of a trial at law to recover the taxes imposed on individuals, would neither suit the exigencies of the public nor promote the convenience of the citizens. It would often occasion an accumulation of costs, more burdensome than the original sum of the tax to be levied.
